translationRepairs: Dingguo wished to execute his minister Ying, magistrate of Feiru. The people of Ying and others reported Dingguo.
Dingguo wished to execute his minister Yingren, the magistrate of Feiru. Yingren and others reported Dingguo.
肥如令郢人 names the magistrate Yingren; the second 郢人 is the same person reporting Dingguo, not a place-collective “people of Ying.”
Dingguo wished to execute his minister Ying, magistrate of Feiru. The people of Ying and others reported Dingguo.
Dingguo wished to execute his minister Yingren, the magistrate of Feiru. Yingren and others reported Dingguo.
Literal English must likewise treat 郢人 as the personal name Yingren throughout, as confirmed by the singular silencing of 郢人 in the next sentence.
In the Yuanshuo era, the brothers of the man from Ying again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
In the Yuanshuo era, Yingren's brothers again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
郢人昆弟 means the brothers of Yingren, continuing the personal name from the preceding units, not “the man from Ying.”
In the Yuanshuo era, the brothers of the man from Ying again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
In the Yuanshuo era, Yingren's brothers again submitted a memorial detailing Dingguo's crimes.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 郢人 as a place origin; Yingren’s brothers is the accurate rendering.
吳王濞 is title plus given name Bi; “Prince of Wu Bi” buries the personal name, while “Bi, Prince of Wu” makes the naming clear.
King Xiaoxiao of Liang was afraid and sent a general against them; they again defeated two Liang armies and the soldiers all ran back.
King Xiao of Liang was afraid and sent a general against them; they again defeated two Liang armies and the soldiers all ran back.
梁孝王 is King Xiao of Liang; “Xiaoxiao” wrongly doubles the posthumous name 孝.
Han bribed Eastern Yue; the Yue king betrayed Liu Bi. When he rode out to review the ranks, assassins ran him through, boxed his head, and relay riders galloped the news to the capital.
Han bribed Eastern Yue; Eastern Yue then deceived Liu Bi. When he rode out to review the ranks, assassins ran him through, boxed his head, and relay riders galloped the news to the capital.
東越即紿吳王 makes Eastern Yue the deceiving agent; inventing a “Yue king” and “betrayed” is not supported.
Jinbei was spared because he had been held hostage.
The King of Jibei was spared because he had been coerced.
濟北王 is the King of Jibei, not merely Jibei, and 以劫故 says he had been coerced rather than held hostage.
The King of Jinbei, on account of having been coerced, was not executed.
The King of Jibei, on account of having been coerced, was not executed.
濟北王 must be romanized King of Jibei; Jinbei is a false reading of 濟北.
